newsitem.title: ITALY: Solana says Russia should not fear NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Solana says Russia should not fear NATO expansion.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana on Friday said Russia had nothing to fear if the western military alliance expanded to include former Soviet bloc countries.
Solana also said "no avenue should be left unexplored" to strengthen ties between NATO and its former Cold War foe, describing Russia as "a key security variable in Europe".

"We can make a credible effort to help bring this country into a Euro-Atlantic security community," Solana said in a speech to the NATO Defence College in Rome entitled "NATO: Fit for the 21st Century".
"A more comprehensive NATO-Russia partnership is as much in Russia's interest as it is in ours," he added.

Russia has staunchly opposed NATO plans to expand its membership to take in former Warsaw Pact countries, citing security concerns, but has recently indicated it does not want the issue to hinder a new relationship with the alliance.
"Russians can be reassured that NATO's enlargement will not pose a military threat to them or to anybody," Solana said.
He also said any concern about the stationing of nuclear weapons was misplaced.
"We have no intentions, no plans and no reason to alter our existing nuclear deployments which, in any case, have been hugely reduced and withdrawn in recent years," he said.
Solana said he believed Russia was beginning to soften its position regarding expansion of the 16-nation alliance.

"Russia must ask itself a key question: 'Is a central and eastern Europe that remains nervous and obsessed with its strategic vulnerability really preferable to a situation where these countries are safely anchored in a multi-national security framework?'," he said.

"It is my impression that Russia is finally coming around to realise all this," Solana said. "This would lift the roadblock of mistrust that kept our relations from running their natural, positive course for so long."
Solana's statements precede two important appointments regarding NATO-Russian relations in coming weeks.

The secretary-general is scheduled to meet Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov in Vienna on September 20 while Russian Defence Minister General Igor Rodionov has accepted an invitation to attend an informal meeting of NATO defence ministers on September 25 and 26 in Bergen, Norway.

They will discuss a proposal made earlier this month by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to draft a formal charter to frame NATO-Russia relations which would make Moscow a full partner in building a new Europe.
Christopher said a NATO meeting to name new members will be held in the spring or summer of 1997 and called for the charter with Russia to be ready for the same summit.
